title: Colors
description: Many strong examples highlight color words such as yellow, orange, and purple, often describing an object in a story.

title: Bowls and containers
description: Bowls stand out in mixing, serving, eating, and washing. Related containers such as baskets, jars, cups, and pans also activate.

title: Comparisons of degree
description: Comparative words such as more, less, better, greater, and bigger stand out, especially after intensifiers such as much or far.

title: Many and several
description: Quantity words such as many, numerous, several, and various stand out when describing a collection or a range of things.

title: Months in dates
description: Month names activate strongly in descriptions of when an event happened.

title: Heavy
description: The word heavy often activates in descriptions of weight, equipment, and heavy metal music.

title: U.S. states
description: State names such as Wisconsin, Arkansas, Missouri, and Illinois stand out in place descriptions.

title: Hearing something
description: Strong examples often highlight heard when someone notices a sound, voice, or piece of news.

title: Pleasure and enthusiasm
description: Words such as pleased, excited, loved, and love frequently receive strong activations.

title: Marriage
description: Married stands out in accounts of spouses and relationships, including biographical passages.

title: Going home
description: Home stands out when someone returns, walks, or is carried back to where they live.

title: Rooms and bedrooms
description: Room and bedroom stand out when characters are inside, enter, or return to a room.

title: Chemical substances
description: Names of elements and compounds, including lead, titanium, chromium, and boric acid, are prominent in strong examples.

title: The Olympics
description: Strong examples discuss the Summer or Winter Olympics and Olympic competition.

title: Mom
description: Mom and mommy stand out in children talking to or about their mother.

title: Surprise and shock
description: Surprised and shocked often stand out in reactions to an unexpected event.

title: Parts of the body
description: Words for body parts and organs, such as eyes, hands, stomach, heart, and brain, often light up.

title: Snacks and refreshments
description: Having a snack or drink stands out, including examples involving coffee, lunch, cookies, and milk.

title: Choices and decisions
description: The feature often highlights choice and decision when describing options or actions people decide to take.

title: Accidents and mistakes
description: Accidentally and mistake often light up when someone knocks over, breaks, or does something unintentionally.

title: Code indentation
description: Runs of spaces used to indent code are especially strong examples. Whitespace is a model token too.

title: Meal time
description: Dinner and lunch stand out when someone is called to eat, with weaker related examples about food and meals.

title: Measurable quantities
description: Words naming quantities, such as concentration, frequency, temperature, height, and length, stand out.

title: Programming languages
description: Language and languages often activate in discussions of programming and computer science.

title: A little bit
description: Little and a bit stand out when describing a small amount or degree, such as a little easier, worried, or closer.

title: Where something is located
description: Located and situated stand out in descriptions of where a place or building can be found.

title: Effects and contributions
description: Words such as contribute, help, impact, and affect stand out when something changes an outcome. The effect can be helpful or harmful.

title: Trains and rail travel
description: Train and trains often activate in descriptions of journeys and rail transport.

title: Tools and implements
description: Strong examples highlight tools such as shovels, axes, spades, scissors, and measuring tape. Other implements, including looms, can activate too.

title: Historical wars
description: Strong examples mention wars in military history, especially the Civil War and the World Wars.
